cause.summary: On PDB186 our model gets ACC 66.13 and AUC 74.44 against the paper's 80.00 and 87.40, below DBPPred (76.88, 79.29). No identity threshold for the homology filter brings it back: AUC stays between 74.4 and 76.0 for thresholds of 25 to 99%, and only training on the unfiltered benchmark, which shares 42 chains with PDB186, reaches 81.49 (87.46 with UniRef90 PSSMs). The paper does not report how many chains its filter removed.

cause.summary: Our largest pair weights are (G,G), (G,D), (G,P) and (N,P). (R,R) and (R,P) have no positive descriptor weight at all (pair weight 0, tied last), and (P,R) and (A,R) rank 133 and 176 of 400. Products of raw log-odds scores do not grow with arginine content (two negative R scores multiply to a large positive), and no variant of Eq. 12 we tried brings the four pairs to the top. Read as a linear grey scale, the published Fig. 2A itself puts (R,R), (P,R) and (R,P) on top and (A,R) eighth (published_values.json, fig2).

assumptions.what: The DNA-binding region is the set of residues of 1AKH chain A with a heavy atom within 4.5 A of a DNA heavy atom
assumptions.sensitivity: R25 and R26, the (R,R) lg 1 occurrence, are 13.2 A from the DNA, so any cutoff below 13 A gives the same split; if the region is the span from the first to the last contact (residues 12 to 59), all five occurrences fall inside it.

cause.summary: The five occurrences come back; the text gives three of their lags off by one ((R,R) lg 3 for lg 2, (P,R) lg 2 and 3 for lg 3 and 4). Whether all five lie in the DNA-binding region depends on how the region is drawn, which the paper does not say: by contact with the DNA in the crystal structure, (R,R) lg 1 (R25, R26), which the text calls very close to the DNA, is 13.2 A away, so four are in and one is out; by the span of contacts, all five are in.

exceptions.evidence: figure-reproduction/output/run/arithmetic.json: Table 4 gives 80.00 - 76.90 = 3.10; the third decimal of 3.105 has no source

cause.summary: On PDB186 our model gets ACC 66.13 and AUC 74.44 against the paper's 80.00 and 87.40, below DBPPred (76.88, 79.29). No identity threshold for the homology filter brings it back: AUC stays between 74.4 and 76.0 for thresholds of 25 to 99%, and only training on the unfiltered benchmark, which shares 42 chains with PDB186, reaches 81.49 (87.46 with UniRef90 PSSMs). The paper does not report how many chains its filter removed.
